records.name: Receptor
records.tldr: Receptors connect molecular recognition to a cellular response through several mechanisms. Their presence and their activity are separate findings.
records.summary: Receptors can be on the surface or inside a cell. Ligand-gated ion channels regulate ion passage; G-protein-coupled receptors act through G proteins; enzyme-linked receptors can contain an enzyme or recruit a separate one. Intracellular nuclear receptors can regulate transcription with cellular partners. A surface signal can ultimately alter genes, while nuclear-receptor family membership does not fix every molecule permanently in the nucleus or require every effect to use new transcription.

HER2 is an orphan receptor without a known direct activating ligand. Its partner HER3 binds neuregulin. Antibody binding, disruption of an assembled complex and inhibition of activation are separate outcomes; the mutant-complex results do not define every antibody response in an unmodified tumour.

In a selected cell-edge example, a G-protein-coupled receptor binds a ligand outside the cell and couples to a G protein on the cytoplasmic side. A separate ligand-gated channel has a ligand-binding site and a pore for ions; the chosen open state and inward arrow do not make every binding event open a channel or determine every ion's direction. A hypothetical probe that remains outside can reach an exposed binding site, while a different entering ligand can reach an intracellular receptor and, in a selected route, influence nuclear gene regulation. These are examples of access and relay, not an exhaustive receptor taxonomy or a universal permeability rule. They do not measure receptor abundance, growth dependence or treatment benefit.

records.name: Myoepithelial cells and the breast basement membrane
records.tldr: Myoepithelial cells are living cells around normal breast ducts and acini; basement membrane is separate extracellular material outside them.
records.summary: These layers help organise normal breast structures and support pathological assessment of invasion. Their location, morphology, staining controls and diagnostic context matter more than a single positive or negative marker.

notes: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.

Basement membrane beneath an epithelial structure differs from plasma membrane around one cell. Cell polarity describes different inward and outward organisation. Gudjonsson and colleagues' human-cell culture experiments showed that normal myoepithelial cells or laminin-1 could restore luminal orientation in collagen gels; this is model evidence about organisation, not a demonstrated cancer treatment.

Myoepithelial immunohistochemistry is supporting evidence interpreted with morphology. p63 is nuclear; calponin and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain are cytoplasmic markers. Ask which cells stain, where they stain and whether technical controls work. A failed positive control undermines an apparently absent rim.

Werling and colleagues found gaps around some noninvasive structures, stromal staining with muscle-associated markers and p63 staining in some carcinoma cells. Gusterson and colleagues found basement-membrane proteins in some invasive carcinomas. Neither marker absence nor protein presence alone proves the tissue boundary. Basal-like RNA features also do not establish myoepithelial ancestry.

In Gusterson and colleagues' 1982 tissue study, laminin and type IV collagen were detected in normal breast, benign lesions and grade I invasive carcinomas but were absent from grade II and III infiltrating carcinomas in that study. That historical cohort does not make protein presence proof of an intact noninvasive boundary, or protein absence a universal grade rule.

Werling and colleagues examined 85 breast lesions. In that series, at least focal p63 staining in tumour cells occurred in 11% of cases, while stromal myofibroblasts stained with smooth muscle myosin heavy chain in 8% and calponin in 76%. Some noninvasive structures had gaps. These assay- and cohort-specific observations explain why localisation and controls matter; they are not universal diagnostic accuracy estimates.

CAP's morphology-based histological classification and supporting-marker assessment answer a tissue question. A schematic rim is neither an immunostain result nor a diagnosis; illustrated gaps or colours cannot establish invasion. Interpret the actual tissue architecture and appropriately controlled stains together.

records.name: Apoptosis
records.tldr: Apoptosis is a regulated process that dismantles a cell. Whether the dying cell stimulates protective immunity is a separate question.
records.summary: The mitochondrial route uses BCL-2-family control of BAX and BAK and cytochrome c release. In cell experiments, combined BAX and BAK loss blocked mitochondrial responses to several apoptotic stimuli; this does not establish resistance to all forms of death. Death-receptor signals provide another route. Apoptosis is not inherently immune-silent: anthracycline-treated tumour cells showed calreticulin-dependent immunogenicity in mouse experiments. A death marker, a mitochondrial response and sustained killing answer different questions. Protein abundance alone cannot establish dependence or choose a treatment.

notes: Intrinsic apoptosis involves mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilisation, cytochrome c release into the cytosol, apoptosome assembly and caspase-9 activation upstream of executioner caspases such as caspase-3 and caspase-7. Death-receptor signalling can activate caspase-8; BID cleavage links this route to mitochondria. Initiator and executioner roles differ.

The BCL-2 family contains survival proteins, including BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1; BH3-only stress mediators, including BIM, BID and PUMA; and pore-forming effectors BAX and BAK. In experimental cells, loss of both BAX and BAK blocked several mitochondrial apoptotic responses, rather than every possible form of death.

Cytochrome c moves from the mitochondrial intermembrane compartment, including crista stores, across the outer membrane to the cytosol. It does not begin in the matrix. The inner membrane separates these compartments; the spatial sketch is simplified, with no implied pore stoichiometry.

A stain for BCL-XL measures abundance rather than survival dependence. BCL2 and BCL2L1 are different genes, and inhibitor selectivity matters. Souers and colleagues re-engineered dual BCL-2/BCL-XL inhibition into BCL-2-selective ABT-199, sparing human platelets; early tumour lysis in three refractory chronic lymphocytic leukaemia patients does not establish benefit in every tumour. A mitochondrial response, caspase marker, sustained killing and immune protection remain separate outcomes. Keep cell identity, timing, handling controls and later survival or regrowth with cleaved-caspase assays, membrane readouts and microscopy. Mitochondrial BH3 challenges test readiness under a defined protocol, rather than completed killing or clinical benefit.

Compare mechanism, morphology, immune consequence and living arrest separately. Apoptosis uses regulated dismantling; necrotic morphology describes boundary failure; ferroptosis requires iron-dependent lipid damage causing death; immunogenicity requires a compatible adaptive response; senescence is a living arrest. These categories are not mutually exclusive outcomes or a universal appearance-based classifier.

In the fictional killing experiment, rescue by both an iron chelator and a lipid-protecting compound with no caspase-inhibitor rescue supports a ferroptosis hypothesis. Check lipid damage, death timing, perturbation specificity and GPX4 or glutathione-related mechanisms before attribution; immunogenicity is a separate test. A single stain is not enough.

records.name: Autophagy
records.tldr: Autophagy delivers cellular material for breakdown and reuse. The amount present, the rate of recycling and whether cells need it to survive are different questions.
records.summary: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in autophagosomes for lysosomal delivery and breakdown. LC3 abundance alone cannot distinguish increased formation from reduced removal. Tandem fluorescent LC3 reporters exploit different responses to acidic and degradative conditions to examine maturation in cell experiments; interpretation requires appropriate controls. Flux and survival dependence need separate tests. In a randomised phase 2 trial of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. A drug trial does not by itself establish selective autophagy dependence in a tumour.

notes: Leading programmes: Amaravadi (Penn) on autophagy inhibition trials; Kimmelman (NYU) on PDAC autophagy and MHC-I; Der (UNC) on KRAS/autophagy.

Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. A controlled short lysosomal block and complementary tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter can help examine turnover and delivery to acidic compartments. Equal starting amounts can have different later fates. Little additional accumulation can reflect a late block, low formation or an unsuitable window; it does not establish dependence.

Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. Lower mTOR signalling can change initiation without guaranteeing completed degradation. Typical research outputs include normalised LC3-II band intensity, reporter compartments per cell and selected-cargo disappearance over time. Tested cultures are consumed or perturbed, and prolonged lysosomal inhibition can itself disturb the system. No universal LC3 or flux cutoff selects treatment.

In Karasic and colleagues' randomised phase 2 study of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel increased response rate but did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. Response was 38.2% versus 21.1%; 12-month survival was 41% versus 49%. These group results do not show selective autophagy dependence or recommend this combination.

Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and the RB1CC1-encoded protein FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

Yamamoto and colleagues found that the cargo receptor NBR1 helped direct MHC-I proteins to lysosomes through an autophagy-dependent route in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma models. This lowered the amount of MHC-I at the cell surface, where it displays antigens to CD8 T cells. In mouse experiments, reducing MHC-I or depleting CD8 T cells reversed tumour control after genetic autophagy inhibition. Chloroquine increased surface MHC-I but, alone, did not significantly reduce tumour weight in the reported experiment; its effects on lysosomes are broad. These model results do not establish that every KRAS-driven cancer depends on autophagy or that blocking it benefits patients.
records.analogy: A recycling station can hold a large pile because more material arrives or because processing has slowed. The pile is an amount; material processed over time is a rate. Neither alone tells you whether the city depends on that station.
interventions: Clinical drug studies and mechanistic dependence tests answer different questions.
Assess flux, selected cargo and survival separately with complementary controls.

records.name: Ferroptosis & regulated cell death
records.tldr: Ferroptosis is a form of cell death involving iron-dependent membrane-lipid damage. General oxidative stress or one positive marker does not establish this mechanism.
records.summary: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation and death. Cystine uptake through system xc- can support cysteine and glutathione availability; it does not transport glutathione itself. GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides, while FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q-associated defence. Dependence on these routes varies with the model and cellular conditions. Establishing the mechanism requires appropriately controlled measurements of death, lipid damage, iron dependence and rescue, with complementary perturbations. Findings in persistent or mesenchymal model cells do not establish a universal vulnerability or a treatment recommendation. Necrotic appearance, danger signals and adaptive antitumour immunity are separate questions.

Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.

GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides to lipid alcohols. FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q radical-trapping defence; it does not replace every GPX4 function or describe the whole protection network. Protein abundance alone does not measure protective activity or predict compound sensitivity.

Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

A culture with abundant GPX4, a general oxidation signal and no death has not demonstrated ferroptosis. Cell-line and xenograft vulnerabilities do not establish tolerable exposure, selective cancer killing or benefit in patients. Alternative defences can confer resistance, so a strong antioxidant programme is not automatically a treatment vulnerability.

Hangauer 2017 investigated reversible drug-tolerant persister states across specified cancer-cell and drug models. Surviving the original treatment could coexist with increased GPX4 dependence; this was not necessarily permanent genetic resistance. The breast model BT474 is HER2-positive, not a triple-negative model. In the mouse relapse experiment, A375 melanoma cells had genetic GPX4 loss, with ferrostatin protection withdrawn while dabrafenib and trametinib continued. Prevented relapse in that setting was not systemic treatment with a GPX4 inhibitor: the authors noted poor systemic pharmacokinetics of RSL3 and ML210. These experiments do not establish a tolerable human window or universal persister vulnerability.

A fictional GPX4 experiment combines lipid oxidation before death, rescue by an iron chelator and a lipid-radical trap, and a corresponding phenotype after an independent genetic perturbation. These observations converge on an iron-dependent lipid-damage explanation; none alone proves it. Include vehicle, rescue-only and an unrelated death condition because rescue compounds can affect other processes. Survival of an otherwise matched FSP1-high comparison is compatible with a parallel defence; directly testing that defence is needed before assigning compensation to it. Energy production, a general oxidation dye and an antioxidant transcript are different measurements and cannot substitute for this causal sequence.
records.analogy: Ferroptosis is rust. Iron plus oxygen eats through the cell's membranes unless an antioxidant crew (GPX4) keeps repainting them. Cells that changed shape to dodge chemotherapy have thinner paint.

records.name: Immunogenic cell death
records.tldr: Immunogenic cell death is regulated cell death that can initiate adaptive immunity against the dying cells in a suitable host and context. Injury alone does not establish it.
records.summary:
The 2020 consensus defines immunogenic cell death through the adaptive immune response, not merely the appearance of dead cells. Antigens, appropriately timed danger signals, antigen-presenting cells and a responsive host all matter. Apoptotic or other death machinery does not by itself classify the immune outcome.

Calreticulin exposure, ATP or HMGB1 release and interferon-related signals are useful mechanistic readouts, but none alone proves protective immunity. Functional cross-priming and appropriate in-vivo immune tests address later steps. The consensus distinguishes mouse vaccination models from established disease; neither a surrogate marker nor a positive mouse assay establishes clinical benefit in a person.

notes: In a local-treatment study, follow injury and signals through presentation, priming, recognition and measured tumour outcomes. Circulating cytokines or proliferating T cells alone do not establish tumour-specific killing, distant control or an optimal radiation dose.

Immunogenic cell death is regulated death capable of initiating antigen-specific adaptive immunity in a compatible responding host. Antigenicity and appropriately timed adjuvant signals are both necessary considerations. It is an immune consequence, not an exclusive machine opposed to apoptosis or necrotic appearance.

Surface calreticulin, released ATP and HMGB1 have distinct mechanistic roles in defined experiments. Calreticulin supported dying-cell uptake, ATP signalled through dendritic-cell P2X7/inflammasome pathways, and HMGB1/TLR4 supported processing and presentation. These are examples rather than a universal sufficient three-marker checklist. A DAMP is not automatically a tumour-specific antigen.

In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Compare later challenge with living matched tumour cells in vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts, and test specificity with unrelated compatible tumour cells. Incidence and growth are functional readouts. Immune-competent versus deficient comparisons alone cannot isolate immunogenic death from other immunostimulation. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Residual inducer, contamination, incompatible antigens and poor death confirmation can invalidate attribution. No universal DAMP cutoff establishes immunogenicity.

Death plus extracellular ATP does not establish a cancer vaccine. Danger signals, cross-priming, functional protection, distant control and patient benefit are separate claims. Even a positive mouse vaccination assay remains model-bound and does not select a clinical treatment.

records.name: Necrosis
records.tldr: Necrosis describes cell and tissue breakdown with loss of membrane integrity. The appearance alone does not identify its cause.
records.summary: Necrotic appearance can follow overwhelming injury or regulated death mechanisms. A late membrane-integrity measurement cannot reconstruct the preceding death sequence. Histology describes the sampled region; necrosis there does not establish the absence of viable tumour elsewhere, treatment success or a particular molecular pathway. Distinguish tissue appearance from a mechanism established by controlled perturbation and complementary readouts. Inflammation and antigen-specific adaptive immune protection are separate outcomes.

notes: Necrosis describes loss of membrane integrity and tissue breakdown, rather than one molecular route. Overwhelming injury, regulated mechanisms and late secondary necrosis after apoptosis with inadequate clearance can converge on membrane loss. Necrosis is broader than necroptosis.

RIPK3-dependent MLKL activation is an example regulated necrotic mechanism. Sun and colleagues used biochemical and cellular perturbations to establish MLKL downstream of RIP3; a necrotic region or membrane-impermeant dye alone cannot establish that pathway.

Histology describes the sampled region; viable tumour may remain elsewhere. A membrane-compromised fraction, qualitative tissue necrosis and method-defined necrotic area answer different questions. Handling, delayed fixation and late sampling affect interpretation, and no universal necrosis percentage identifies a death mechanism or proves treatment success. Preparing and staining a section consumes tissue, while live-cell dye assays use tested aliquots and report a defined membrane-compromised fraction. Clinical morphology and experimental pathway perturbation have different validation contexts.

HMGB1-deficient necrotic cells produced less inflammation in defined experiments. That result concerns danger signalling, rather than automatic adaptive immune memory. Dye entry after an intervention cannot establish necroptosis, vaccine activity or clinical benefit without the separate causal and host tests.

records.name: Cellular senescence
records.tldr: Senescent cells remain alive while their division is durably arrested. Their effects depend on the cells, signals and surrounding tissue.
records.summary: Senescence is a stress-associated cell state with durable cell-cycle arrest and other context-dependent features. Identifying it requires combined measurements rather than one marker. In genetically switchable blood-cancer models, release from senescence allowed renewed division with enhanced clonogenic potential. That experimental result does not predict that every senescent cell will restart or that a person will relapse. Arrest, secretion and effects on neighbouring cells require separate assessment. Model findings do not establish a preferred senolytic treatment.

Senescent cells remain alive and metabolically active while division is durably arrested. Damage, oncogenic signals and treatment stresses can induce the state. It is distinct from death, reversible quiescence, the broader concept of dormancy and immune exhaustion, and is not a synonym for a person's age.

Low proliferation and increased p21 one day after stress do not establish durable senescence or a harmful secretory programme. Combine cell identity, longitudinal arrest or regrowth assessment and complementary features such as p16, p21, damage markers and senescence-associated beta-galactosidase. Fixed tissue cannot test later recovery, and no universal marker or arrest-duration cutoff works across contexts. Research outputs include method-defined cell fractions, marker intensities and longitudinal proliferation or regrowth. Stained sections and tested cells consume material. Secretions and their functional effects require their own readouts rather than inference from an arrest marker.

The senescence-associated secretory phenotype varies with cell, stimulus, timing and environment. In Coppé and colleagues' culture experiments, selected secretions promoted epithelial invasiveness; in Demaria and colleagues' mouse skin wounds, senescent cells and PDGF-AA supported repair. Neither experiment establishes a universal harmful mixture or a clinical instruction to remove senescent cells.

Genetically switchable blood-cancer models showed enhanced clonogenic growth after release from senescence. This supports possible escape in those systems, not inevitable restart, relapse prediction or a preferred senolytic treatment. Arrest, secretion and effects on neighbouring cells require separate tests.
records.analogy: A workshop can stop making copies while continuing to use energy and send messages. The messages and their effects must be measured in context.
interventions: Experimental induction, persistence and clearance require separate measurements.
Model findings do not establish a preferred senolytic treatment.

records.name: Ubiquitin-proteasome system & protein homeostasis
records.tldr: Ubiquitin can change a protein's interactions, location or fate. Some tags support proteasomal destruction; tagging alone does not establish completed degradation.
records.summary: E1 enzymes activate ubiquitin, E2 enzymes carry it and E3 ligases help select substrates and assemble modifications. Chain architecture and cellular context influence the result; ubiquitination is not universally a destruction signal. Deubiquitinases can remove or remodel tags, and proteasomal degradation is a later process that needs its own evidence. A protein can fall because synthesis changes, cells are lost or degradation increases, so abundance alone does not identify the route. In targeted-degradation experiments, target binding, E3 recruitment, protein loss, proteasome dependence and sustained cellular effects are distinct observations. Proteasome inhibitors and recruited-degradation strategies intervene at different steps; mechanistic measurements do not by themselves establish clinical benefit.

Suitable tagged cargo can be unfolded by ATP-dependent proteasomal machinery and broken into fragments, while ubiquitin is removed and reused. Other ubiquitin signals organise interactions rather than destruction, and yeast experiments show overlapping chain functions. Lysosomal autophagy and proteasomal breakdown are distinct routes.

Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. Measure named-substrate decay over time with synthesis, handling and viability controls; restoration of an E3 adaptor can strengthen attribution without proving direct binding or global proteasome failure. Catalytic activity per time, ubiquitinated-cargo intensity and protein lifetime in hours are different readouts. KEAP1 is one CUL3 adaptor for NRF2, so a CUL3 change cannot uniquely identify that substrate. Pulse labelling or a controlled temporary synthesis block can help estimate turnover but may cause stress. Independent perturbation and restoration help distinguish a selected-substrate effect from a secondary response; enzyme engagement alone does not establish selective killing.

This historical clinical result does not make an arbitrary E3 variant or abundant protein a predictive treatment biomarker.

Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.

records.name: BRCA1 / BRCA2 (HRD)
records.tldr: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A reported variant, inherited cancer risk, remaining gene copies and current repair function need separate interpretation.
records.summary:
BRCA1 and BRCA2 name genes everyone normally carries. Interpret a reported variant by its classification, sample and origin, then assess the remaining allele and repair function. An uncertain BRCA2 variant with no normal sample and no remaining-copy assessment establishes neither inheritance nor biallelic loss nor current repair deficiency. Tumor purity and complex copy-number states can limit allele interpretation.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. Purified full-length human BRCA2 promoted RAD51 assembly on single-stranded DNA in Jensen 2010. These model-specific results do not determine the effect of every human variant; the matching-template diagram omits many preparation and finishing steps.

In the CIMBA analysis, the invasive-breast-cancer results included 3,797 BRCA1 and 2,392 BRCA2 carriers, with individual marker data available for varying subsets. Among tumors with relevant marker information, 68% in BRCA1 carriers and 16% in BRCA2 carriers were triple-negative. These are pathology proportions among cancers in mutation carriers, not the chance that an individual carrier develops cancer or that a person with triple-negative disease carries a BRCA variant. Age and ascertainment matter.

Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

records.name: DNA damage response & homologous recombination
records.tldr: Cells detect DNA damage, coordinate repair and adjust their cell cycle. A damage signal is different from completed repair, and a repair-gene finding alone does not predict treatment benefit.
records.summary:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

records.name: HRD genomic scar scores (GIS, LOH, HRDetect)
records.tldr: These scores measure selected patterns of accumulated chromosome change. The assay and cutoff matter; a high score alone does not establish current repair failure or treatment eligibility.
records.summary:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

notes: A composite score compresses selected features of a tumour's chromosome history. Like a summary of past events, it leaves details out; like numbers on differently calibrated scales, the same numerical value need not have the same meaning in two laboratories. The composite count is not a percentage of repair-deficient cells. Copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity can replace two parental versions with copies of one version without reducing the total copy number, so loss of heterozygosity is not always loss of a physical chromosome copy.

Telli 2016 selected the boundary of 42 using an independent training set of 497 breast and 561 ovarian cancers, including 78 breast and 190 ovarian cancers classified as lacking a functional BRCA1 or BRCA2 copy. That classification used a deleterious variant with loss of the other copy, two deleterious changes in one gene, or BRCA1 promoter methylation with loss of the other copy. The boundary was the fifth percentile among these BRCA-deficient cancers, aiming to capture about 95 per cent, rather than an optimised divider of drug responders. Some deficient cancers therefore fall below it. The study's abstract and discussion use at least 42, whereas its Methods prints greater than 42; a result at the boundary needs the actual validated assay rule, not an improvised inequality.

Telli tested the unweighted LOH plus TAI plus LST score in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials, using a high score or a deleterious or suspected-deleterious tumour BRCA1/2 alteration. A variant of uncertain significance did not count as a mutated BRCA result. The odds ratios for minimal residual disease, residual cancer burden class 0 or I, were 4.96 in PrECOG's platinum, gemcitabine and iniparib cohort and 10.18 in the pooled two cisplatin cohorts. These associations are not three randomised demonstrations of extra platinum benefit. PRIMA later defined HRD positivity by a tumour BRCA mutation or a MyChoice genomic instability score of at least 42. That trial definition and current prescribing conditions are separate facts.

ARIEL2 Part 1 used a prespecified 14 per cent genomic-LOH cutoff in relapsed, platinum-sensitive high-grade ovarian cancer. Of 206 enrolled patients, 204 received rucaparib and 192 could be classified: 40 BRCA-mutated, 82 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-high and 70 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-low. Twelve BRCA-wild-type tumours lacked enough neoplastic nuclei for the LOH classification. This percentage of genome is a different quantity from the composite sum, and a single-arm rucaparib study cannot by itself separate prognostic association from differential treatment benefit. HRDetect is different again: its weighted sequence-signature logistic model outputs a probability of BRCA-deficient genomic history. Its 2017 sensitivity and AUC describe that classification task, not an individual's chance of benefiting from a medicine.

In the GeparSixto analysis, HRD was measurable in 193 of 315 triple-negative breast cancers. Pathological complete response rose from 33.9 to 63.5 per cent with added carboplatin in the HR-deficient group and from 20.0 to 29.6 per cent in the other group. The treatment-by-HRD interaction had P = 0.327. This does not establish that the treatment effects differ by HRD status, nor does a non-significant interaction prove they are identical. In TNT, 376 people with advanced triple-negative disease or a germline BRCA-associated breast cancer received carboplatin or docetaxel. Germline-BRCA carriers had response rates of 68 versus 33 per cent, with interaction P = 0.01; a high Myriad HRD score did not select extra carboplatin benefit. Association with response and evidence for choosing between treatments are different questions.

PAOLA-1 randomised 806 people with advanced ovarian cancer responding to first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy plus bevacizumab. Both maintenance groups received bevacizumab; the added treatment was olaparib or placebo. The 2019 HRD-positive progression-free-survival hazard ratio was 0.33, with a 95 per cent interval of 0.25 to 0.45. The olaparib label's planned exploratory HRD-negative analysis gives 1.00, with an interval of 0.75 to 1.34. That interval is compatible with a range of effects and does not prove exactly zero benefit. It also cannot be transferred to an unrelated assay, breast cancer, a different drug or olaparib without bevacizumab.

PRIMA's 2019 analysis randomised 733 people after response to first-line platinum for advanced ovarian cancer. Among 373 with HR-deficient tumours, median progression-free survival was 21.9 versus 10.4 months with niraparib versus placebo, hazard ratio 0.43 with a 95 per cent interval of 0.31 to 0.59. In the overall population it was 13.8 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.62 with an interval of 0.50 to 0.76. These are historical progression-free-survival results, not an updated overall-survival estimate. The U.S. niraparib label effective July 2026 restricts first-line maintenance to HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to platinum, selected with an authorised companion test.

The U.S. olaparib label effective July 2025 permits olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance for adults with HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum; the specified HRD definition includes a deleterious or suspected-deleterious BRCA alteration and/or genomic instability, with an approved companion test. Its early-breast indication instead requires a deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA alteration, HER2-negative high-risk disease and prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, with the approved test. A tumour-only BRCA finding or an arbitrary high scar number does not substitute for these conditions.

The specimen and analysis are part of the result. Telli used tumour DNA, a genome-wide SNP panel, allele-imbalance profiles and prespecified counting rules; if the score failed and BRCA testing was negative or failed, HRD status was undetermined. A failed result is not a low score. Reports should identify the assay version, usable tumour content, DNA input/quality, copy-number and allele-balance method, segmentation, and purity/ploidy assumptions. HRDetect was explored in a small biopsy series and one formalin-fixed specimen with substantial sequencing artefact; those demonstrations do not certify every degraded specimen. RAD51 foci ask a different, conditional question about present repair. A BRCA reversion or 53BP1 loss is not itself a measured new scar score or proof of restored function.

In a fictional report, laboratory X gives a score of 48 and a paper uses laboratory Y's cutoff of 42 in early triple-negative breast cancer. The numerical comparison 48 > 42 does not establish HRD positivity on X's assay: its scale, quality requirements and validated boundary are needed. Even on the correct scale, association with response to one regimen does not establish extra carboplatin benefit over a comparator. GeparSixto's interaction analysis and TNT's high-score result illustrate that distinction; neither permits a blanket claim that a high-score tumour never benefits from carboplatin.

records.name: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)
records.tldr: Homologous recombination deficiency means that a template-guided DNA repair process is impaired. A gene finding, a genomic scar and current repair function provide different evidence.
records.summary:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

records.name: Mutational signature
records.tldr: An inferred pattern of mutations that supports hypotheses about the processes that produced them. Its interpretation depends on the data, comparison patterns and method.
records.summary:
A mutational signature is a distribution over mutation categories inferred from a catalog of calls. It does not attach an observed cause to every mutation. Several processes can overlap, some causes remain unknown, and a classifier of BRCA-related repair deficiency is not a model of a patient's probability of drug response. Its endpoint and validation population must be named.

Single-base substitutions change one base, doublet substitutions change adjacent bases, and indels insert or delete sequence. In a fictional four-category exercise, template A has percentages 40, 30, 20, 10 and B has 30, 40, 20, 10. For 100 mutations, a 50/50 mixture gives 35, 35, 20, 10; a 60/40 mixture gives 36, 34, 20, 10. The close reconstructions illustrate ambiguity; these are arithmetic examples, not fitted SBS3 data or observed biological results.

HRDetect combines six weighted features, including microhomology-associated deletions, substitution signatures 3 and 8, rearrangement signatures 3 and 5 and a scar index. It is not simply an SBS3-positive call. In the original study, applying genome-trained weights to exome-like data reduced sensitivity to 46.8%; retraining improved it to 73% while adding calls not made by the genome model. Missing rearrangements and sparse substitutions are consequential, so panel, exome and whole-genome implementations require separate validation, uncertainty and fit checks.

Roberts analyzed 954,247 mutations across 2,680 exomes from 14 cancer types; the APOBEC pattern reached 68% of mutations in some samples, not in every breast cancer. HRDetect reported 98.7% sensitivity and 124 high-scoring tumors among 560 breast cancers, about 22%, under its study definition. That selected cohort estimate is not a population prevalence or a clinical response probability. DNA quality, variant-calling errors, signature competition, catalog and software versions remain part of interpretation.

records.name: Double-strand break repair: HR versus end joining
records.tldr: Cells can repair breaks through both DNA strands using a matching template or several end-joining routes. The available template, cell state and broken ends affect which route can operate.
records.summary:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

records.name: DNA replication stress
records.tldr: Replication stress means difficulty copying DNA. Slowed forks, damage responses and dependence on a checkpoint are different observations.
records.summary:
Replication stress concerns difficulty copying DNA, including slow or stalled forks. A stalled fork can be protected and restart; it is not automatically a broken chromosome. Checkpoint activation, recovery, incomplete copying, damage and death are separate stages and measurements. High checkpoint-gene RNA or rapid proliferation alone does not establish fork stress, dependence or drug sensitivity.

RPA coats exposed single-stranded DNA and helps recruit ATR through ATRIP, initiating checkpoint signaling in biochemical and cellular experiments. Activated H-Ras in normal human-cell models produced hyper-replication before damage signaling and senescence. Bester studied HPV E6/E7 or cyclin-E-driven models in which nucleotide limitation disturbed replication and nucleoside supplementation in culture improved dynamics. These experiments do not recommend supplements or predict the behavior of every oncogene-bearing tumor.

In a fictional DNA-combing exercise, live cells receive a 30-minute IdU pulse followed by a 30-minute CldU pulse. At the stated example stretching calibration of 2 kilobases per micrometre, a 7.5-micrometre second track represents 15 kilobases copied in 30 minutes, or 0.5 kilobases per minute; a 15-micrometre track gives 1 kilobase per minute. Bester used those pulse times and calibration, but these example lengths are not that study's results and the calibration is not universal.

DNA-fiber measurements require viable cells that incorporate labels; extraction destroys sampled cells. Ordinary fixed pathology cannot retrospectively supply live-label tracks. Document pulse timing, labeling, stretching, track selection, cell-cycle distribution, model and comparison group. A lower population S-phase fraction is distinct from the speed of one selected molecule. Track length alone establishes neither the cause, breaks, restart nor death; checkpoint dependence needs a targeted perturbation and a separate functional outcome, without a universal patient-positive cutoff.

At a moving replication fork, the unopened parental duplex lies ahead of the junction. New complementary DNA accumulates behind it on the parental templates. One new strand is made continuously toward the advancing fork; the lagging strand is made in short pieces that are later joined. Both are synthesised in the 5-prime to 3-prime direction. A shorter labelled track at the same pulse duration describes less DNA copied along the measured molecule, rather than a shorter labelling interval or proof of chromosome breakage.

records.name: Lipid synthesis, uptake & cholesterol
records.tldr: Cells can make, import, store and reuse lipids. The route they use and their dependence on it vary with the cell and conditions.
records.summary: Lipid metabolism includes synthesis, uptake, storage, membrane remodelling and oxidation. Cholesterol regulation and fatty-acid regulation overlap but are not interchangeable. Identify the SREBP member, cellular compartment and measured output rather than treating a transcript, precursor, nuclear fragment, sterol amount and synthesis rate as the same observation. SCAP-SREBP transport responds to endoplasmic reticulum cholesterol in the cited cell experiments. The mevalonate pathway supplies sterols and nonsterol products, including substrates for protein prenylation. Rescue by mevalonate therefore cannot uniquely identify cholesterol as the limiting product. Transcript abundance, lipid abundance, labelled production and a controlled survival-dependence experiment answer different questions. Results from a particular cell model or mouse experiment do not establish a universal tumour vulnerability or a preferred diet or treatment.

notes: SCAP and local endoplasmic-reticulum sterol conditions regulate transport of membrane-bound SREBP to the Golgi. Processing releases a fragment that enters the nucleus and regulates lipid synthesis and uptake. Sufficient local sterol supply can retain the complex in the ER; total cellular cholesterol and SREBP RNA do not measure this processing.

In the fictional supply experiment, nuclear SREBP-2 and uptake messages respond to lipid-poor medium; external lipid supply can reduce the response and compensate for synthesis perturbation. Record medium composition, density, timing and viability before assigning dependence. A supply-sensitive state does not establish the response of a person's tumour. Assess precursor and nuclear regulator, responsive transcripts, cellular sterols and uptake separately from labelled synthesis rates. Use controlled supplementation to test the proposed bottleneck; total amount does not specify production or local sensing. Lower synthesis does not itself show that a compound bound its target, and a medium effect does not identify uptake as its cause. An uncharacterised SCAP or MTOR variant needs evidence for its proposed functional effect; a gene name alone assigns neither activation nor loss of function.

In transgenic mice expressing a truncated SREBP-2 construct, Horton and colleagues observed preferential activation of cholesterol synthesis over fatty-acid synthesis in liver and adipose tissue, contrasting it with earlier SREBP-1a results. They separately measured transcripts and synthesis using labelled water. These are relative effects in a named experimental system, not exclusive duties of each family member or proof that a transcript measurement equals flux. Precursor location and nuclear processing require their own measurements.

Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.

HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. Cholesterol amount, sterol synthesis and the whole mevalonate pathway are therefore different measurements. SCAP-SREBP sterol sensing regulates synthesis and uptake, but its activity, pathway transcripts, metabolite supply and dependence must each be established in the tested cells and medium.

Freed-Pastor 2012 studied mutant-p53 breast cancer cells in three-dimensional culture, with different outcomes in two triple-negative lines. Depleting mutant p53 reduced invasive behaviour in MDA-MB-231 but did not make it form ordered hollow acini; MDA-MB-468 could acquire a more ordered, hollow architecture. Statins reduced invasion in the former and caused growth inhibition with extensive death in the latter, rather than exactly reproducing every p53-depletion phenotype. Mutant-p53 depletion reduced mevalonate-pathway expression, and mevalonate add-back opposed several statin effects. This supports a pathway contribution in the studied systems without isolating cholesterol. The whole paper also examined growth, death and xenograft growth; it was not solely an architecture experiment, and none of these results established patient treatment benefit.

The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. That is not evidence that GGPP rescues inhibition of the transferase itself, nor that every effect in both cell lines was entirely explained by one metabolite. The authors allowed contributions from other products. In a fictional supply comparison, synthesis falls under an inhibitor in both lipid-poor and lipid-rich medium, but growth slows mainly in the former while import is stipulated to compensate in the latter. Equal engagement with different growth outcomes is compatible with environmental supply; it is not a measurement of supply or dependence in a person's tumour.

In the selected SREBP-2 route, the precursor spans a membrane and its gene-regulating end faces the cytosol. SCAP escorts the membrane-bound precursor from endoplasmic reticulum through transport vesicles to Golgi membranes. Cleavage releases the regulatory fragment into cytosol before nuclear entry; it does not carry the whole precursor, SCAP or the vesicle into the nucleus. Local sterol sensing and Insig-associated retention regulate this transport. A schematic of the route supplies neither a universal sterol threshold nor a measured transcription rate.

records.name: Endoplasmic reticulum stress and the unfolded protein response
records.tldr: Cells respond to strain on protein folding through several signalling branches. A response does not by itself establish cell death.
records.summary: The unfolded protein response has distinct outputs. IRE1-dependent processing of XBP1 RNA produces a potent transcriptional regulator; total XBP1 message and its spliced fraction are different measurements. PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and can reduce translation initiation. ER stress also promotes ATF6 proteolysis, releasing a fragment that acts in the nucleus. These findings come from molecular and cell experiments. Branch activity, adaptation, survival dependence and treatment benefit require separate evidence. Specify branch, timing, total protein or RNA controls and direct growth and death measurements.

notes: ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

ATF6 travels from ER to Golgi for processing; the released fragment, rather than the intact membrane-bound precursor, acts in the nucleus. Total XBP1 RNA differs from its splice-form fraction. Other kinases can phosphorylate eIF2alpha, so one phosphosite cannot identify the whole response.

Specify preserved material, RNA quality, isoform-specific methods, total-protein controls, timing and identified cell populations. Splice-form fractions, processed ATF6 and defined phosphoprotein signals are different outputs. Increased XBP1 splicing with stable viable-cell counts supports a branch response, not lethal stress; measure growth and death directly and test causality independently. RNA or protein preparations and compatible tissue stains use material; functional dependence tests require viable cells. Report splice-form fractions, defined phosphosite signals or processed fragments with assay-specific controls, rather than a universal UPR-positive treatment threshold.

XBP1 depletion altered tumour growth and relapse in defined triple-negative breast cancer models, with an HIF1alpha transcriptional interaction. Model findings and patient expression-signature associations do not establish universal XBP1 dependence, an assay cutoff or a treatment benefit. Successful stress adaptation can support survival.

records.name: Oxidative phosphorylation
records.tldr: Oxygen use and cellular energy production are related measurements. Researchers need controlled experiments to work out how much energy a cell produces through mitochondrial respiration.
records.summary: Extracellular flux methods estimate respiratory and glycolytic contributions to energy production under defined assumptions. A respiratory message, measured oxygen use, calculated energy output and dependence for survival are distinct claims. Normalisation, fuel, viable-cell input, collection time and the specified method version belong with a result. Electron transport, proton pumping, return through ATP synthase and uncoupling are distinct steps. The mitochondrial matrix and intermembrane space locate the two sides of the inner membrane; naming these compartments does not supply a universal conversion ratio.

notes: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

The fictional oxygen-rate example gives 60 minus 30 = 30 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 viable cells after ATP-synthase inhibition. This is an inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference, not picomoles of ATP, a death percentage or a corrected ATP-production calculation. Fuel, normalisation and assay controls remain attached.

In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. The matrix-facing F1 part uses the transferred energy to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Protons provide the driving force; they are not converted into ATP. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. In Racker and Stoeckenius' reconstituted vesicles, a light-driven membrane system from Halobacterium supported ATP formation when mitochondrial ATPase was included. Their artificial vesicles pumped in the opposite direction to the intact source cells, so the experiment supports coupling without specifying a universal cellular orientation or ratio.

Extracellular acidification can include respiration-derived carbon dioxide as well as glycolytic acid production. Keep correction assumptions, normalisation and method version with any calculated ATP rate. The 2018 correction to Mookerjee and colleagues' 2017 method changes the ATP-linked oxygen-rate equation and reports use of a different hyperpolarization factor in some calculations; several numerical rates changed while the authors retained their qualitative conclusions. An inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference is therefore not itself an ATP rate, and an unversioned fixed conversion should not be inferred.

In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

Echeverria 2019 treated three patient-derived triple-negative breast cancer xenograft models with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Barcode structure was broadly maintained at the residual nadir; regrowth could select dominant barcodes, so this does not exclude all clonal selection. In PIM001-P, the RNA analysis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation and isolated residual cells had higher oxygen consumption and lower extracellular acidification than untreated cells. Those rate measurements were not obtained in every model. IACS-010759 delayed regrowth after chemotherapy in the three tested models, rather than eradicating the tumours. Regrown models could again respond to chemotherapy. Two serial human biopsy cases supported stability during initial AC but did not establish invariant clones through all subsequent treatment. Rate, state, perturbation response and clinical benefit remain distinct evidence.

Yap 2023 reported phase 1 IACS-010759 studies in 17 people with acute myeloid leukaemia and 23 with advanced solid tumours. Elevated blood lactate and neurotoxicity limited exposure needed for sustained complex-I inhibition; target inhibition was modest, antitumour activity limited, no recommended phase 2 dose was established and both studies were discontinued. These named safety and exposure results separate a model vulnerability from a usable treatment. A respiratory RNA signature plus a lower ATP-based signal still establishes neither increased oxygen-consumption rate nor counted cell death. Measure identified viable cells, normalised oxygen use, engagement and independent growth or death outcomes. Acidification can include respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolysis, and lactate production with oxygen can coexist with respiration.

A mitochondrion has an outer membrane and a folded inner membrane. The space between them is the intermembrane space; the matrix is enclosed by the inner membrane. Each membrane is a phospholipid bilayer, with two leaflets rather than being a single leaflet of a shared membrane. Electron transfer ends with oxygen reduced to water, while some complexes pump protons across the inner membrane. These distinct processes do not give a universal conversion from oxygen use to ATP production.

records.name: Androgen receptor
records.tldr: The androgen receptor can bind androgen hormones and regulate gene activity. Receptor staining, an RNA subtype and dependence on the receptor are different findings.
records.summary:
The full-length androgen receptor is a hormone-binding protein that can regulate transcription. Its interactions with other proteins, receptor form and cellular setting affect its activity.

Receptor amount, location, transcription and growth dependence are different observations. Nuclear AR immunostaining reports protein in sampled cells; a luminal androgen receptor, or LAR, label is a versioned RNA-classifier result. TBCRC 032 correlative analyses found AR protein expression alone insufficient to identify AR-dependent tumors. Neither staining nor classifier membership alone proves patient benefit.

Full-length AR has distinct regions for transcriptional regulation, DNA binding and ligand binding. Androgens can change receptor interactions, nuclear localization and regulatory-DNA binding, with effects determined by partners, accessible DNA and receptor form. Tran's antiandrogen experiments in prostate models tested binding, nuclear movement and transcriptional effects separately. An RNA signal does not characterize a truncated protein or transfer those prostate results to breast-cancer treatment.

A fictional tumor with 20% AR-positive nuclei but a non-LAR RNA classification need not have a mistaken result. The assays measure different layers; compare antibody, scoring, tumor-cell content, preservation, sampling, normalization and classifier version. Twenty percent stained nuclei is not twenty percent of patients expected to respond. Dependence requires a controlled receptor perturbation with downstream and growth or survival measurements.

Lehmann 2016 refined TNBCtype from six classes to four tumor-specific classes after immune and stromal contributions explained the former immunomodulatory and mesenchymal stem-like signals. LAR does not mean estrogen-receptor-positive disease. TBCRC 032 was a defined phase Ib/II metastatic breast-cancer study of enzalutamide with or without taselisib, with phase II focused on AR-positive TNBC; its exploratory correlations do not turn an RNA subtype into a universal treatment rule or import a prostate indication.

records.name: BRD4
aka: BET bromodomain proteins (BRD2, BRD3, BRD4, BRDT)
records.tldr: BRD4 reads acetyl marks on DNA-packaging proteins and helps regulate transcription. Blocking a recognition pocket and removing the whole protein test different functions.
records.summary:
BRD4 is a chromatin reader that recognizes acetylated histones and helps regulate transcription. Its recognition pockets and other protein interactions can contribute different functions.

Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. records.name: Notch signalling
records.tldr: Notch receptors can relay signals between contacting cells. The effect depends on the receptor, ligand, alteration and tissue; receiving a signal does not by itself prove growth dependence.
records.summary:
A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.
